The system combines the car's own internal sensor readings with outside conditions such as weather and road quality. The authors tested the approach in four stages, from controlled simulations to a real-world pilot across several countries. Their work aims to close the gap between laboratory results and performance on actual roads. Most current vehicle health tools depend mainly on internal data gathered through on-board diagnostics ports, such as engine temperature, fault codes and vibration.

Those tools generally ignore the surrounding stresses a car faces every day. The authors found that adding contextual information improves the prediction of component failures. The system uses nine internal mechanical measurements along with driver behavior, environmental factors and interaction terms, for a total of twenty-three variables. Pavement roughness is monitored at fifty hertz with an inertial measurement unit, and weather and road data are updated within a sixty-second window. In a simulation built on two thousand vehicle-month observations, the full contextual model reached a macro F1-score of 0.855.

Removing the environmental features lowered that score by 0.026, and relying only on internal mechanical data produced an F1-score of 0.807. Removing the internal signals caused a much larger drop to 0.655, which the authors say confirms that internal measurements remain the core of failure prediction. To test the method on real industrial data, the team used the AI4I 2020 benchmark of ten thousand milling-machine records, where the model reached a macro F1-score of 0.814 and an area under the curve of 0.973. Performance was strongest for heat dissipation failures at 0.972 and weakest for random failures at 0.497. The field pilot covered five privately owned vehicles driven in Germany, India and Brazil, which together logged 992 trips and roughly one hundred thirty million sensor observations.

Wear was checked against service records and physical measurements of brake pads and tire tread. Across six wear-driven events, the framework detected every one, though fine-tuning each vehicle's model roughly halved the timing error, from 25.9 days to 12.2 days. The authors also reported clear limits: the Brazilian Toyota Etios produced an average error of about 206 days per event, and predictions for scheduled preventive maintenance had a mean error of 93.5 days, since the algorithm tracks physical wear rather than calendar intervals. Shapley analysis confirmed that environmental factors such as rain and road roughness contribute to the predictions. The article ends by noting structural limitations and outlining priorities for future research.

Articles.Title: AI Vehicle Maintenance System Merges Environmental Context With Internal Sensor Diagnostics

stories.Headline: Feeling AI in Fashion Retail: Mixed Effects on Employee Creativity
stories.Summary:
A study published in Fashion and Textiles on November 8, 2026, found that emotionally responsive artificial intelligence, often called "feeling AI," does not uniformly boost creativity among fashion retail employees. The researchers, led by Ishtehar Sharif Swazan, reported that the psychological effects depend on the context and on which AI features are involved. Some features raised employees' confidence in their creative work, while others produced anxiety that changed how they approached creative tasks. The authors stressed that this distinction matters for an industry that depends on human innovation and aesthetic judgment.

The study examined two capabilities of feeling AI, anthropomorphism and personalization, and how they shape creative self-efficacy and job replacement anxiety. Those psychological states in turn affect two forms of creativity: proactive creativity, which is self-initiated, and responsive creativity, which is prompted by outside demands. The researchers treated AI as a psychological stimulus rather than only a technical tool. The survey covered 302 professionals working in U.S. fashion retail across buying, merchandising, planning, forecasting, marketing, product development, and customer service. The sample was 55.6 percent female and 43.7 percent male, and most participants held a bachelor's degree and had four to six years of experience.

The researchers analyzed the data with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling, and the model explained 22 percent of the variance in creative self-efficacy and 14.1 percent in proactive creativity. The results showed that anthropomorphism significantly reduced creative self-efficacy while also significantly increasing job replacement anxiety. Personalization strongly boosted creative self-efficacy, though its hypothesized effect on reducing job replacement anxiety was not statistically significant. Creative self-efficacy predicted proactive creativity, and job replacement anxiety significantly increased responsive creativity without significantly reducing proactive creativity. Subgroup analyses found that personalization varied by job function, with planning and forecasting roles reporting more of it than customer service, while the other mechanisms were consistent across departments.

The study notes several limitations, including its cross-sectional design, which limits causal conclusions, and its U.S.-only sample, which may not generalize globally. Sales, marketing, and customer service staff were more heavily represented than design and merchandising professionals. For managers, the authors suggest favoring personalized, adaptive tools over highly human-like agents, investing in training that builds creative self-efficacy, and communicating openly about how work is changing. The research adds to the literature on human-AI collaboration by focusing on psychological effects rather than operational utility. The authors call for future work to test the model across cultural contexts and to study the effects of AI integration over time.

Articles.Title: Feeling AI in Fashion Retail: Mixed Effects on Employee Creativity

stories.Headline: Fire hawks inspire encryption and AI pairing to guard healthcare cloud data
stories.Summary:
Researchers have published a two-layer security system for healthcare cloud data that combines an encryption scheme with a machine-learning screen for access requests. The framework, called OFHXOR-PSL, appeared as an open-access paper in Discover Computing and was tested on two Internet of Health Things datasets. It reported a detection accuracy of 95.68 percent and a security level of 98.56 percent, with an attack level of 4 percent. The work is described in an article dated November 8, 2026, which was reported by Scienmag.

The system addresses a concern that hospitals face as they store electronic medical records on third-party cloud infrastructure. The authors say that common tools such as AES, RSA, and ECC, along with standard classifiers, can be computationally inefficient and weak at spotting threats. Their approach treats encryption and intrusion detection as one jointly designed pipeline instead of two separate tasks. The encryption layer uses XOR with a key chosen by the Fire Hawks Optimizer, a method modeled on birds of prey, and each session gets its own key. The paper reports an average key entropy of 7.94 bits per byte, close to the theoretical maximum of 8.

The second layer screens every request to reach stored records. A gateway extracts features such as IP address, query pattern, access frequency, session duration, and a geolocation anomaly score, then passes them to an ensemble of three classifiers. If uncertainty exceeds a threshold of 0.45, the request is blocked as suspicious. The authors also say the detection module keeps learning after a malicious classification, which they describe as a way to handle new attacks. The experiments used the WUSTL-EHMS-2020 and ECU-IoHT datasets, and the proposed ensemble outperformed artificial neural network, K-nearest neighbors, and support vector machine baselines.

The authors state that the research was carried out by A. CG, A. C, and R. Neerukonda, and they acknowledge several open questions. They note that key distribution assumes a pre-established secure channel such as TLS 1.3, and that user authentication and trust management were not tested experimentally. They also say that ciphertext integrity would need separate protection, for example with an HMAC, because XOR offers no diffusion. Future plans include post-quantum key encapsulation based on CRYSTALS-Kyber, federated learning, and validation on more datasets. The source code is openly available on GitHub under an MIT licence.

Articles.Title: Fire hawks inspire encryption and AI pairing to guard healthcare cloud data

stories.Headline: Hybrid AI Model Predicts Postoperative Lung Function from Preoperative CT Scans
stories.Summary:
A team of researchers has developed a hybrid artificial intelligence model that can estimate how well a patient's lungs will work after surgery, using only a routine preoperative CT scan. The study, published in European Radiology Experimental in 2026 and reported by bioengineer.org on November 8, 2026, was led by Wang, Sun, Ma and Li. The model combines transfer-learned deep neural representations with elastic net regression to predict forced vital capacity and forced expiratory volume in one second, without requiring preoperative lung function tests or detailed surgical planning. The researchers say it is aimed at patients with pulmonary nodules who may undergo lobectomy, segmentectomy or wedge resection.

The motivation is that lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide, and rising detection of nodules has increased the number of thoracic operations. Surgeons must weigh removing enough tissue to treat the disease against preserving functioning lung. The traditional segment-counting method works only for anatomical segmentectomies and lobectomies, not wedge resections, and it depends on baseline spirometry while often overestimating functional loss. The study used data from 105 surgical patients at Huadong Hospital affiliated to Fudan University, drawn from 7,494 screened between October 2014 and October 2023, with 61 women and 44 men averaging 65.4 years old, and a separate external cohort of 31 patients from Heilongjiang Provincial Hospital treated between January 2017 and January 2023. In external testing, the hybrid model outperformed four alternative approaches and the segment-counting method, with a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.707 for forced vital capacity and 0.729 for forced expiratory volume in one second.

The authors, Wang, Sun, Ma and Li, presented the approach as an automated tool to support individualized decisions in common thoracic resections, though they were careful to describe its limits. Their own summary, paraphrased here, is that the study was retrospective, that the sample was modest because postoperative spirometry is not routinely performed, and that the clinical inputs were limited to six basic parameters. They concluded that larger prospective multicenter studies with standardized postoperative testing will be needed before the tool can be used in surgical practice. The article does not report any regulatory review or clinical rollout, so the model currently remains a research finding.

Articles.Title: Hybrid AI Model Predicts Postoperative Lung Function from Preoperative CT Scans

stories.Headline: Security AI Agent Outperforms GPT and Claude
stories.Summary:
Cogent Security, a California-based AI security startup, drew attention this month after its model VR-1.1 outperformed models from Anthropic and OpenAI on a public benchmark. The article, published by The Elec on November 9, 2026, reports that VR-1.1 scored 57.9 percent accuracy across 190 CVEs on LiveCVEBench. Claude Code, powered by Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, and Codex, based on OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Cyber, each reached 45.3 percent. A CVE is a system of unique identifiers assigned to publicly disclosed software and hardware security vulnerabilities.

The benchmark measures how well AI coding agents can independently analyze and fix CVEs. VR-1.1 begins by reading vulnerability reports and source code, then generates test code to reproduce the flaw. Once the flaw is reproduced, it traces the affected code paths and applies a targeted patch. It then runs a separate review to check for new weaknesses and generates regression tests to prevent the bug from returning.

The company's cofounders include two former employees of Abnormal Security, an AI-based email security firm, and a third founder with experience at Coinbase and Blackstone. Cogent says every patch includes diagnostic results, proof-of-concept code and records of executed tests so security teams can review fixes quickly. The article notes, however, that VR-1.1 was less efficient on cost, using about 2.23 million tokens and 31 turns per successful task. Claude Code used about 380,000 tokens and 8.4 turns, and Codex used about 684,000 tokens and 15.3 turns.

The article cautions that these results come from a single benchmark and do not establish overall superiority. LiveCVEBench is designed to stop models from memorizing published answers, so it compares against baseline model versions trained before the relevant CVEs were disclosed. Newer models may have absorbed recent patch records and open-source commits into their training data, so results could differ on newly disclosed CVEs. The article also notes that when accuracy is tied, the agent using fewer tokens ranks higher.

Articles.Title: Security AI Agent Outperforms GPT and Claude - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: How I Fight AI Brain Fry
stories.Summary:
The author, writing on sergeykuhne.com on November 8, 2026, describes a problem many people face when working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex from the terminal. Running several tasks at once means each agent reply pulls them into another tab, and the constant switching eventually exhausts the brain, breaks focus, and leaves them unsure where they started or what remains. Other advice, such as taking breaks or limiting scope, is mentioned, but the author has tried a different approach. They identified two core problems, sequencing and context, and organized their work along the lines of a priority queue.

The queue lives in git, with each ticket stored as a markdown file in the repository beside the code it concerns, and the board's state kept as a committed snapshot. An agent cycles through the board to research new tickets, build those a human has marked as safe, run tests and a browser check, and verify deployed work. Sensitive changes are built on a branch with approval requested first, and the agent never deploys to production, which the author keeps for themselves. Items needing human judgment are gathered into an owner inbox, where a script ranks them.

The author reads them through a Claude artifact, a page rebuilt from git each cycle, and records verdicts back onto the ticket card in git. The author says closing each item returns its context to the queue, so the next item can be approached with focus. The article notes that the work remains tiring, and that the main difficulties have been the tooling that delivers context quickly and the risk of tickets looping while they wait for a ruling only the author can give. The author calls the system a living project that is still being improved and says it has produced a large gain in productivity.

Articles.Title: How I Fight AI Brain Fry

stories.Headline: Chinese AI Matchmaker Refunds Fees If You Don't Marry in 3 Years
stories.Summary:
A Chinese artificial intelligence matchmaking service is attracting attention for offering a full refund of membership fees to users who do not marry within three years. Liangpei AI launched the service in July, and Hong Kong's South China Morning Post and other foreign media reported on it on the 9th. Members pay 2,000 yuan, roughly 400,000 to 410,000 won, and can recover the full amount if they have not married after three years. The company holds the fees in a separate bank account and says it will not record them as revenue until the refund window closes.

The service differs from typical dating apps in both its goal and its structure. Instead of keeping users logged in and chatting, it aims to help them find a spouse quickly and leave the platform. New members spend about 20 minutes in a voice conversation with an AI that covers family, upbringing, education, work, interests, personality and views on marriage. The system then scores compatibility and offers one candidate at a time, and a member must end the current connection before seeing the next match. Applicants must give their real names and photographs and pass a check that they are single, and the company says that in the first month its verification screened out more than 150 married people trying to join.

Founder Zeng Xinxun created the service because, in his view, existing apps show only limited details such as age and occupation, which makes it hard to judge a person's real character. He argued that a longer conversation with an AI can capture personality, daily habits, family background and marriage expectations. He also said that having too many options may mean the algorithm has failed to identify a suitable match. The company's refund window reflects its own research, since its team surveyed 150 couples at a Shenzhen marriage registration office and found that more than 70% had married within three years of first meeting.

The service comes amid a slump in China's marriage market, which the articles tie to a tough job market and high housing and child-rearing costs. China registered 6.76 million marriages last year, up 10.8% from a year earlier but about half the 12.25 million recorded in 2015, according to Ministry of Civil Affairs data. Registrations in the first half of this year fell 7.5% from a year earlier to 3.28 million. The company said it had more than 9,300 active users as of September, 57% men and 43% women, while SCMP later reported that sign-ups had topped 35,000 with about 9% becoming paying members. The company has also raised 15 million yuan, roughly 3 billion won, in angel funding.

Articles.Title: Chinese AI Matchmaker Refunds Fees If You Don't Marry in 3 Years - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: In Case You Missed It: A.I./Data Center Articles - NewClips From Last Week - November 9 - PA Environment Digest Blog
stories.Summary:
PJM Interconnection filed a revised reliability backstop generation procurement proposal with FERC, according to the PA Environment Digest roundup posted on October 31, 2026. The grid operator wants to hold its next auction in March 2027 with a price cap of $555 per megawatt-day. stories.Headline: IBM Ties AI Agent Governance to a Five-Year Tennis Deal and a Raised Cash Target - ad-hoc-news.de
stories.Summary:
IBM has extended its partnership with the United States Tennis Association by five years, a deal announced on 28 October that keeps the Armonk-based company as the official artificial intelligence and cloud partner of the US Open through 2031. The renewal came alongside a wider product push covering agent identity controls, quantum hardware and post-quantum cryptography. It also followed a refreshed financial outlook the company published on 21 October. On 27 October IBM unveiled enterprise features for identifying and governing AI agents, including tools for agent discovery, verified identities, access controls, and ways to assess how well those agents perform inside corporate systems. The company said several of these capabilities are now generally available, while others remain in preview.

The agent identity and administration focus had first been flagged about two weeks earlier at its TechXchange event. Confluent, an IBM-owned company, added updates to its Streamhouse architecture to keep the business data that agents and analytics rely on current. On the hardware side, IBM introduced a Quantum System Two in Chicago on a Friday, describing it as operational at the Hyde Park Labs site and its most advanced system available. It is IBM's first quantum machine in Illinois and runs on the Quantum-Nighthawk processor with 120 qubits. A day earlier IBM, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD launched a joint development platform for quantum error correction, with a first phase linking IBM quantum computers to the research centre's Umbra system, which uses AMD processors and graphics chips.

The effort supports the US Department of Energy's Quantum Genesis Mission, and IBM has also packaged IBM Quantum Safe as one suite to help enterprises manage their move to post-quantum cryptography. The financial backdrop came in third-quarter 2026 results published on 21 October, which reported revenue of $17.1 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $2.95. Management kept its full-year outlook for currency-adjusted revenue growth at 4% to 5%, but raised its free cash flow growth target so that the metric is now expected to rise by more than $1 billion year over year. Taken together, the sponsorship, governance tools and quantum launches show IBM pairing its AI and quantum ambitions with a stronger cash picture, though the articles do not say how these products will affect future sales.

Articles.Title: IBM Ties AI Agent Governance to a Five-Year Tennis Deal and a Raised Cash Target - ad-hoc-news.de

stories.Headline: Google Taps AMD CPUs for New AI Chips Despite In-House Push
stories.Summary:
Google introduced two new artificial intelligence chips on November 9, 2026, as part of an effort to align its hardware with the growing use of AI agents, which are assistants that carry out tasks on their own. The chips are the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i MAX, and they bring the company's 8th-generation TPU family to four products, up from two announced in April. The TPU 8tx is built for small-scale training and inference while protecting personal data, with security functions on the chip itself that guard sensitive information in real time. The TPU 8i MAX links two TPU 8i chips, which are optimized for low-latency inference, to double computing performance and memory bandwidth compared with a single TPU 8i.

The most notable element is that the TPU 8tx uses AMD's 5th-generation EPYC central processing unit, code-named Turin, as its host CPU, which coordinates data movement for the GPU-style processors. AMD said these processors power the host infrastructure of the TPU 8tx, which is the first TPU system to offer hardware-based confidential computing. The move is a departure for Google, which in April 2024 had unveiled its own Arm-based CPU, Axion, and had been installing it alongside its TPUs across its data centers to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs and Intel CPUs. Google Cloud, the unit of Alphabet that leads chip development and data center construction, announced the new products.

Mark Lohmeyer, vice president of AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud, said customers need confidence that their data is securely protected when they deploy AI agents. He said that pairing the 5th-generation EPYC processors with Google's 8th-generation TPU architecture has brought hardware-based confidential computing to Cloud TPUs for the first time. AMD, for its part, said the collaboration combines EPYC performance, its AMD Infinity Guard security software and x86 software compatibility with TPUs. The articles present the choice as reflecting a judgment that EPYC is ahead on security, though that interpretation comes from the reporting rather than from either company.

The shift comes as AMD's position in server CPUs strengthens at Intel's expense. According to Mercury Research, Intel's share of x86 server CPU revenue was 53.8% in the first quarter of this year, while AMD reached an all-time high of 46.2%. Some observers quoted in the reporting suggested AMD could expand its influence further by supplying custom chips through partnerships like the one with Google, in addition to general-purpose CPUs. The articles do not say whether Google will continue to rely on its own Axion chips in other parts of its infrastructure.

Articles.Title: Google Taps AMD CPUs for New AI Chips Despite In-House Push - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Google Taps AMD Chips for New AI Processors Built for Agents

The TPU 8tx is designed for agent security and small-scale training and inference while protecting personal data, with built-in security functions that protect sensitive data in real time on the chip itself. stories.Headline: AI-Written Complaints Swamp U.K. Public Bodies, Some Running 200 Pages
stories.Summary:
Complaints drafted with generative AI are overwhelming public bodies across Britain, according to a Guardian report published on November 9, 2026. Local councils, Parliament and the courts have all seen sharp rises in submissions written with chatbots such as ChatGPT and Claude, with some growing roughly tenfold in length. Deborah Evans, chief executive of Lawyers in Local Government, said the average complaint once ran about two pages but now often reaches around 20, and the longest she has seen ran to 200 pages. These documents sometimes include irrelevant material or cite foreign laws and court rulings that do not apply in Britain. They can also contain so-called hallucinations, where the AI invents laws or rulings that do not exist, forcing officials to verify every claim.

The Information Commissioner's Office said some freedom-of-information requests believed to be AI-written are so long or repetitive that it is hard to tell what the applicant is actually asking. Errors alone do not allow a public body to ignore a complaint, which must still be reviewed and answered under the relevant procedures. Holly Weakens, a senior caseworker in a Labour lawmaker's office, estimated that about half the emails she receives were written with AI, a trend she said began rising in earnest in 2024. GMB, the union representing staff in lawmakers' offices, reported that casework volumes have more than doubled at some offices, with staff repeatedly working beyond contracted hours. Alessandro Georgiou, leader of Enfield Council in London, said more residents are using AI to challenge council decisions, and he described the rise in parking appeals as a serious problem.

Transport for London received 4,769 freedom-of-information requests in the 2025-26 fiscal year, the highest on record and about 5% above the previous peak set in 2023-24. TfL said appeals that appear to be AI-written have increased recently and that some contain technically complex or inaccurate claims. Government figures show about 14,000 new single claims were filed with employment tribunals between April and June this year, up 28% from a year earlier, though the article notes that whether AI is driving the increase has not been established. Several ombudsman offices are capping complaint lengths or redesigning online forms to limit submissions.

Wiltshire Council is considering using AI to summarize long emails and draft initial replies. The British government has issued guidance telling civil servants to verify information generated by AI tools, avoid entering personal data, and leave final decisions to people. The article also notes that AI can help citizens who previously struggled to write complaints gain better access to administrative procedures. Public bodies are now weighing how to protect the right to complain while coping with the surge in work.

Articles.Title: AI-Written Complaints Swamp U.K. Public Bodies, Some Running 200 Pages - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Nvidia Supplies 90% of AI Servers. Spy Scandal Tests Its Governance
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged an extramarital relationship with Elise Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy, a disclosure made on the 8th, local time. The allegations concern whether national secrets were leaked, and the matter has rattled the global chip industry. Huang has said he intends to stay on as chief executive, though lawmakers are pressing for an inquiry. Nvidia's graphics processing units power an estimated 80 to 90 percent of the world's data center servers, which is why the episode has drawn wide attention.

Congressional committees have asked Huang to appear in a closed session on the 18th, the day after Nvidia's scheduled earnings release on the 17th. Sen. Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, said he would pursue an investigation. Nvidia has denied any leak of secrets, and its spokesman said the matter will not slow the company's progress. The company's board plans its own probe through an independent body to examine whether trade secrets reached China and whether any transfer was careless or deliberate.

The company itself is a point of concern because it depends so heavily on one person. About 60 executives report directly to Huang, who monopolizes decision-making, and Nvidia has no formal succession plan. Huang's daughter and son both hold senior roles, and The Information reported that the company was moving toward family management, though the line of succession remains unclear. Analysts such as Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein have described Huang as the company itself. Huang has admitted fault in a letter to employees while saying he would work to win back trust.

Possible outcomes include a board request for Huang to resign or a voluntary departure, along with a criminal inquiry the articles say is a real possibility. A divorce filing could also force a property split, since Forbes estimates his net worth at $154 billion. South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have voiced concern that the affair could prompt tighter U.S. export controls on AI chips to China. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun on the 9th called reports that Huang's partner was a Chinese spy baseless and a smear.

Articles.Title: Nvidia Supplies 90% of AI Servers. Spy Scandal Tests Its Governance - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: iH to Install AI Safety System at New Incheon Housing Complex
stories.Summary:
Incheon Metropolitan City Development Corporation, known as iH, announced on November 10, 2026, that it will install an artificial intelligence-based safety system in its public housing to protect residents from accidents. The move follows recent fires in apartment underground parking garages that heightened residents' anxieties. The agency said the system will be adopted from the design stage of its apartment project at the S2 block in Geomam, Seo District, Incheon. The measure targets everyday spaces such as electric-vehicle charging stations, children's playgrounds, and walkways within the complex.

The system will sound an alarm at an integrated control center, display live footage, and send an immediate text message to managers when an accident occurs or warning signs appear. Electric-vehicle charging stations will get three-stage temperature detection and cutoff technology, which automatically cuts power if the temperature rises above 25 degrees Celsius during charging. Flame and smoke detectors will also be installed in the parking garage. AI-enabled cameras at playgrounds and walkways will detect abnormal behavior such as falls, fainting, or assaults and alert the control room in real time. The system is scheduled to begin full operation when the complex is completed in December 2030.

iH is holding working-level meetings with the Keryong Construction consortium, the builder, to coordinate detailed safety standards. Kim Hak-jong, head of iH's housing welfare division, said that creating a living environment where residents can live with peace of mind is the basic duty of public housing. He said the agency will expand the AI smart safety system to all apartment development projects it pursues going forward, starting with the Geomam complex. The article does not say what the system will cost or how many cameras and sensors will be installed. It also gives no further details on how the expansion will be carried out across other projects.

Articles.Title: iH to Install AI Safety System at New Incheon Housing Complex - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: NH-Amundi Lists ETF Tracking AI Chip Substrate Suppliers
stories.Summary:
NH-Amundi Asset Management said on November 10, 2026, that it had listed the HANARO Samsung Electro-Mechanics Fixed AI Core Substrate ETF on the main board of the Korea Exchange. The fund targets makers of multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) and high-value package substrates, such as flip-chip ball grid arrays (FC-BGA), which are needed in growing volumes as AI systems advance. Samsung Electro-Mechanics, which mass-produces both MLCCs and FC-BGAs, is the anchor holding at a fixed 25% weighting. The remaining 75% is spread across nine Korean companies in the substrate, materials and equipment chain.

Individual holdings are capped at 20%. The fund rebalances back to the 25% target at quarterly scheduled reviews if the anchor's weight drifts with share prices. The nine other stocks are chosen by an AI system built on a large language model, which analyzes corporate filings, news reports and analyst research to score how closely each company ties to the MLCC and substrate industries. Selection combines that thematic score with market capitalization.

As of the end of October, the largest holdings after Samsung Electro-Mechanics were LG Innotek, Doosan, Isu Petasys and Daeduck Electronics, followed by Simmtech, Korea Circuit, Taesung, TLB and Haesung DS. The eligible universe includes makers of package substrates and multilayer boards, plus suppliers of materials and equipment used in substrate production. NH-Amundi Asset Management, led by Chief Executive Kil Jung-sup, launched the product, and Kim Seung-chul, head of its ETF investment division, explained the rationale. Kim said that as AI accelerators and high-performance servers gain computing power, high-capacity MLCCs and ultra-fine substrates that keep power efficiency stable grow more important.

He described the fund as a one-stop vehicle for the whole domestic AI substrate value chain, anchored by Samsung Electro-Mechanics, which he called globally competitive. The articles do not report investor demand, fees or first-day trading results. The launch is framed as a response to surging demand for these components as AI servers become more powerful. The articles do not describe any regulatory action or further steps beyond the listing and the scheduled quarterly reviews.

Articles.Title: NH-Amundi Lists ETF Tracking AI Chip Substrate Suppliers - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute Wins International AI Standard
stories.Summary:
The Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute announced on November 10, 2026 that it has obtained ISO/IEC 42001 certification, the international standard for artificial intelligence management systems. The institute says it is the first public institution under the Korea Forest Service to receive the certification. The standard was set in December 2023 by the International Organization for Standardization and the International Electrotechnical Commission as the world's first such standard for AI management. It assesses whether an organization manages risk, transparency and accountability when it adopts and runs AI. The institute says the certification recognizes its framework and capacity for using AI safely and responsibly.

To meet the standard, the institute has widened its use of AI in public services and internal work tied to arboreta and gardens. It set up AI operating policies and internal management rules, and it added a risk assessment procedure for each AI system. It also raised the quality controls on data used to train and run AI, strengthened protection of personal data, and spelled out which units and roles handle this work. The institute plans to review and improve its AI management framework on a regular basis. Its stated aims are to prevent risks that may arise from AI use and to offer AI services that the public can trust.

The institute's chairman, Sim Sang-taek, is the official who framed the announcement. According to the report, he said the institute will keep providing better arboreta and garden services through transparent and trustworthy AI operations. The article was written by Park Hee-yoon for Seoul Economic Daily and was translated from Korean with AI, so the quotations may not match the original wording exactly. The report does not describe any reaction from outside observers or any penalties or deadlines tied to the certification.

Articles.Title: Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute Wins International AI Standard - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: CalPrivacy expresses support for privacy legislation targeting AI training
stories.Summary:
California's privacy agency said on November 6, 2026 that it would be willing to back privacy legislation aimed at restricting the use of personal data for artificial intelligence training. The statement came from the agency as it explores which legislative topics to sponsor or support in the coming year. The reporting, published by MLex and written by Xu Yuan, presents this as a stance still under consideration rather than a finished proposal. The articles give no details of a specific bill, its text, or its timeline. The agency's position signals interest in limiting how personal information may feed into AI systems during training.

As described, the willingness to support such rules is conditional on the agency's broader legislative planning for the year ahead. The articles do not specify any numbers, deadlines, penalties, or affected categories of data. They also do not name any lawmaker or bill that would carry the measure forward. The statement was attributed to California's privacy agency, the body that oversees the state's privacy rules. The reporting paraphrases the agency's comments rather than quoting specific language at length.

It describes the agency as considering which topics to sponsor or endorse, with AI training data now among them. No further remarks from individual officials appear in the articles. The context is that AI training on personal data has become a focus of privacy concern, though the articles themselves do not elaborate on specific incidents or prior rules. What happens next is not spelled out in the reporting. Any actual legislation would depend on the agency's selection process and on the state's legislative calendar, neither of which the articles describe.

stories.Headline: A gun-control group has plans for safe chatting with AI
stories.Summary:
Everytown for Gun Safety, one of the most influential gun-control organizations in the country, has reportedly made plans for how it will chat safely with artificial intelligence. The article, published by the Washington Examiner on November 7, 2026, centers on this initiative. It is the only detail the piece offers about the plans themselves, so the reporting leaves much unexplained. The article does not lay out what the chatting would involve or what safeguards would be used. Everytown was founded in 2014 through the merger of Mayors Against Illegal Guns and Moms Demand Action.

Over the past decade it has used political spending, litigation, research, and lobbying to push for stricter firearms laws. The article names campaigns for expanded background checks, restrictions on certain firearms, and laws that let courts temporarily remove guns from people deemed dangerous. The article does not say whether the AI plans connect to any of these efforts. The article does not identify any specific person at Everytown who spoke about the plans, and it does not quote a spokesperson. It also does not describe any response from the organization, from AI companies, or from critics.

Without those statements, the piece cannot tell readers who is responsible for the plans or what they have said about them. Beyond the organization's background, the article offers little context about the plans' timing or scope. It does not say whether the plans are underway, how they would be carried out, or what the next steps would be. Readers seeking those details will need further reporting, and the article itself does not indicate what comes next.

stories.Headline: AI and the culture of your firm
stories.Summary:
The article reports on a conversation published by Accounting Today on November 9, 2026, in which Dan Hood, its editor-in-chief, spoke with Sandra Wiley, CEO and chief strategist of Sandra Wiley Strategies, about how artificial intelligence will change the culture of accounting firms. Hood framed the discussion as a look at an area that has received little attention, noting that both the culture firms will have and the culture they build now will shape whether they can make the most of AI. Wiley, a consultant on human capital issues such as culture, recruiting and retention, argued that the profession will need to pay closer attention to culture than it has before. Wiley said that culture is not something that simply appears but something firms can build on purpose, and that AI will shift it in several ways.

She expects trust to be extended to people earlier in their careers, because AI will take over much of the entry-level work that staff used to learn from over three to five years. She also described AI as becoming a partner to staff, so that people and technology together form one culture rather than two separate parts of the firm. Wiley added that productivity outcomes are likely to matter more than billable hours, and that firms will need different roles, profiles and hiring expectations than they have had before. Hood and Wiley agreed that the change will require a higher level of trust and knowledge at every level, including partners, many of whom may be unfamiliar with advisory work.

Wiley said that the entry point into the profession will rise, which means the ceiling of firms will rise too, and she noted that many of the young CPAs she has spoken with want challenging work from the start. Hood pointed out that training newer staff faster to earn trust sooner is a different path from what his own professors described, and that the pipeline of students and new recruits takes years to develop. Wiley said firm leaders will need to run a current firm and a future firm at the same time, and she warned that firms that do not start transforming now could face trouble within a couple of years. The conversation ended with Hood and Wiley noting that the pace of AI change is hard to match with the slower timeline of building the workforce.

Articles.Title: AI and the culture of your firm - Accounting Today

stories.Headline: TCS, Google Cloud Open Gemini AI Experience Centre in Kolkata
stories.Summary:

The articles describe it as a hub where businesses can work on these applications together with the two companies. The facility is also meant to display AI-powered solutions designed for a range of business operations and customer service needs. The articles do not give any figures on investment, staffing, or capacity. TCS and Google Cloud are the two organisations behind the launch, with TechGig reporting the opening. The articles do not include direct statements from executives of either company about the centre's goals.

Their stated aim, as reported, is to strengthen the adoption of agentic AI among consumer businesses. Beyond that, the reporting does not describe further commitments. The launch extends TCS's network of Gemini Experience Centers, which now numbers eight globally. stories.Headline: India’s Office Workforce to Reach 48 Mn by 2030 as AI Reshapes Demand: Report
stories.Summary:
India's office-using workforce is projected to rise from about 38 million in 2025 to 48 million by 2030, according to a study by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield published in November 2026. Under the consultancy's baseline scenario, office employment would grow by nearly 9 million between 2025 and 2030, or about 1.8 million workers a year. The study ties this growth to the expansion of office-based services and global capability centres, which are moving toward higher-value work. The report expects those centres to drive demand for research and development, product engineering and analytics. It also says the shift toward more advanced work will raise demand for well-located, adaptable office space.

The projection comes with a warning that vacancies may rise as new commercial office supply enters the market. The study expects the national office vacancy rate to climb from 14.3 percent in 2025 to a peak of 16.2 percent in 2029, then ease to 15.5 percent in 2030 as new supply levels off. It also argues that India's lower labour costs may limit the immediate business case for AI adoption. Productivity gains from AI are expected to become more visible later in the decade, mainly in IT services and global capability centres. The report describes AI as likely to change the nature of work and the skills employers need, though not necessarily to reduce office space demand.

Anshul Jain, chief executive of Cushman & Wakefield's office and retail business for India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific, is quoted in the study. He said AI would change the nature of work and required skills, but that this does not necessarily lower office demand. Jain also said occupiers will increasingly prioritise quality and flexibility in their office requirements. He said developers and investors will need to adapt to changing workplace needs.

The study's authorship and the consultancy's own forecasts are the source of these figures, and the article does not report any independent verification. The article does not say what happens next beyond the forecast period, nor does it describe any regulatory or policy response. It is a single consultancy study reported by one publication, so the figures reflect a baseline scenario rather than a settled outcome. The projections run through 2030, and the article gives no further timeline for how the vacancy peak or productivity gains will play out.

Articles.Title: India’s Office Workforce to Reach 48 Mn by 2030 as AI Reshapes Demand: Report - Analytics India Magazine

stories.Headline: Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding
stories.Summary:
Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin, a design-and-review layer for AI coding agents, and says thousands of its engineers use it. The plugin makes an agent write a specification before it writes any code, and then fresh subagents with no conversation history attack that spec. The stated goal is to catch wrong assumptions in a Markdown file rather than in a pull request. The package includes 7 skills, 9 reviewer personas, 6 brainstorm lenses and 5 review stages, and it carries no model weights because the agent supplies the language model.

The plugin is an Apache 2.0 collection of skills, reviewer personas and document standards, not a new language model. It runs on any harness that can spawn fresh subagents, including Antigravity, Claude Code version 2.1.271 or later, Claude Cowork, Codex and ChatGPT, and it uses your existing model quota. No accuracy benchmark has been published, so the evidence offered is adoption and end-to-end harness test runs. The method traces to Dave Rensin's essay on elephants and goldfish, and the Google Open Source blog frames it as a fix for AI "slop" and session context collapse. The README says it is not an officially supported Google product.

The workflow splits work between a long-running session, called the Elephant, and stateless subagents, called Goldfish. The Elephant holds project context and drafts the spec without writing code, while each Goldfish reads only the draft and the files it references. The brainstorm command runs a six-lens Goldfish swarm covering YAGNI, token cost, UX, migration, observability and technical debt, and the draft command turns the brief into a design document. A drift-report command later compares code with the spec, and the docs recommend running it weekly. A five-stage Goldfish review then runs an initial zoom-out, a comprehension test, a critic review, an intermediate zoom-out and an implementation-readiness check, with each stage allowing at most one re-audit.

Responsibility for the design rests with the human developer, who resolves trade-offs and approves the design, while Google published the plugin under its open-source program. Among the test results, Codex 0.163.0 completed 15 native fresh-context reviewers in order and passed two live tests in 573.13 seconds, and the Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 run ran 16 native reviewers. The Claude Cowork run stopped after stages five through seven because of a usage limit, and an open issue, number 237, reports that AGENTS.md content leaks into Codex reviewers. The published comparison places EGM beside GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro Specs and Superpowers, and the main cost flagged is heavy token use along with unverified isolation on some hosts.

Articles.Title: Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding

stories.Headline: Which Routing Does Each MoE Model Use? DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral, Llama 4, gpt-oss Compared
stories.Summary:
Two articles from November 8, 2026 cover very different corners of open model work. The first, a MarkTechPost piece, compares how ten open Mixture-of-Experts models route tokens to their experts. It notes that expert counts range from 8 to 384 and top-k from 1 to 8, and that some models keep an always-on shared expert while others drop it. The sources it cites were checked on November 7, 2026.

The comparison is organized around five routing settings: expert count, experts per token, shared experts, the gating function and the load-balancing method. Mixtral 8x7B uses 8 experts with top-2 and a softmax over the selected scores, while gpt-oss-120b uses 128 experts with top-4 and does not disclose its balancing method. DeepSeek-V3 uses a sigmoid score with an auxiliary-loss-free bias, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro raises its expert count to 384 while lowering top-k to 6. Qwen3-235B-A22B uses 128 experts with top-8, and Llama 4 Maverick routes each token to one of 128 routed experts plus one shared expert.

The article attributes these details to each model's Hugging Face configuration files, model cards and technical reports. It notes that the Qwen3.6 and Llama 4 materials omit gating details, and that gpt-oss and Llama 4 omit their balancing methods. The author also says that Kimi K2 keeps the DeepSeek-V3 router design while raising routed experts to 384, and that the Kimi K2 report found higher sparsity lowered loss at fixed active compute. The article's stated takeaway is that configuration files make routing auditable, but labels such as "17B active" can hide quite different routers.

The second source, a GitHub repository called llama-modchip at version 2.4.0, takes a different angle on the same model family. Its README claims it can run the 284-billion-parameter DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a CPU workstation with 64 GB of RAM and no GPU, reporting a 56.56 GiB checkpoint on disk and 57.61 GiB peak resident memory at a 256K context. The project reports 44.36 tokens per second for CPU prefill and between 9.1 and 14.7 tokens per second for generation. It requires a custom quantization type, GGML_TYPE_Q2_0, so the models will not open in unpatched llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio. The README lists installation through a single script or a pre-compiled binary bundled with its Hugging Face repositories.

Articles.Title: Which Routing Does Each MoE Model Use? DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral, Llama 4, gpt-oss Compared

stories.Headline: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)
stories.Summary:
I can't write this as a news story, since these are technical guide articles, not breaking news, and the rule requires me to follow the paragraph structure exactly. The articles do carry enough detail for a proper write-up, so I'll attempt the three-plus paragraph version, with each paragraph at four or five sentences. The MarkTechPost guide, published November 8, 2026, explains seven routing strategies used to decide which expert networks process each token in Mixture-of-Experts models. The router scores every expert, keeps the top candidates and weights their outputs, so only a small subset of experts runs for any given token.

The article describes how Mixtral 8x7B gives each token access to 47 billion parameters but uses 13 billion active ones. It notes that routers in current models choose from as few as 8 experts, as in Mixtral, up to 384, as in DeepSeek-V4-Pro. The guide organizes its coverage around the main approaches, starting with top-k routing, where each token scores all experts and keeps the k highest. Switch Transformer routed each token to a single expert and showed that quality held while router compute fell.

The article also covers shared-plus-routed designs from DeepSeekMoE, in which always-on shared experts hold common knowledge so routed experts can specialize. It describes sigmoid scoring with bias-based balancing, used by DeepSeek-V3, which adjusts a per-expert bias after each step without adding interfering gradients. The guide reports that loss-free balancing reduced a load imbalance measure from 0.72 to 0.04 at the 1-billion-parameter scale. The article also explains expert-choice routing, a Google approach in which each expert picks its top tokens so every expert receives a fixed bucket size.

It reports more than 2x faster training convergence for that method, but warns that it can leak information from later tokens in causal models. The guide attributes one measured abnormal loss drop of roughly 10 percent to that leak. The article presents these as trade-offs rather than settled winners, and it describes sigmoid gating with bias balancing as the dominant recipe among 2026 frontier open MoE models. It also notes that serving-time load fixes remain necessary even with the best router design.

Articles.Title: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)

stories.Headline: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B that Cuts Qwen3.8-27B Propaganda From 22% to 0.9%
stories.Summary:
Nous Research has released Arete-27B, a 27-billion-parameter open-weight model built by supervised fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B. The article says the model is designed to strip Chinese state framing from the base model's answers. On Nous's own 803-prompt evaluation, the share of answers containing propaganda fell from 22% to 0.9%. The weights, the evaluation and the training data are all publicly available under an Apache 2.0 license, matching the base model.

The fine-tune changes only the model's answers on politically sensitive topics, according to the article. Nous used no reinforcement learning, no preference optimization and no architectural changes. Training covered about 52.8 million tokens at a 64,000-token context over two epochs and 1,202 steps, using a teacher model called Inkling from Thinking Machines, which Nous chose because it is open and avoids distillation restrictions. The released training set contains 34,878 prompts across seven topics, with 29,236 accepted teacher answers forming the supervised split. Nous reports that the fact score on its evaluation rose from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5, and that answers scoring zero dropped from 359 to 216.

Nous Research is the developer, and the article attributes the base model to Alibaba's Qwen team. Nous's team said it observed refusals, deflections and Chinese government-aligned answers on sensitive topics in the base model. It selected Qwen3.8-27B because it was the most capable local model and showed the behavior it wanted to change. Nous also said it removed every training prompt that overlapped with its evaluation, and that the evaluation and its grading scripts are released under the MIT license.

The article reports that general capability held steady on Nous's tests, with Hermes Bench moving from 65.77% to 65.60%, which Nous calls noise. Terminal-Bench-2.1 rose from 67% to 70% in Nous's own harness. The article notes that the largest gain came in freedom of expression, where propaganda fell from 60% to 1%. Its comparison table places Arete-27B alongside Qwen3.8-27B, Muse Glimmer 30B and Gemma 4 31B on fact score, propaganda rate and footprint. The article does not describe any further steps or planned updates.

Articles.Title: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B that Cuts Qwen3.8-27B Propaganda From 22% to 0.9%

stories.Headline: 36Kr Exclusive: Heavy-Duty Physical AI Startup Secures Nearly 400 Million Yuan Financing Within 1 Year of Establishment – Core Team Ex-Huawei & Li Auto, 100+ Vehicles in Operation
stories.Summary:
Shanghai EABOT Technology Co., Ltd. (EABOT), a heavy-duty industrial physical AI company founded in February 2026, has recently completed two consecutive financing rounds totaling nearly 400 million yuan, according to a 36Kr exclusive published on November 6, 2026. Investors named in the report include Ge Weidong, Chentao Capital, Hony Capital, Zero One Auto, Xingfu Capital, and Starq Fund under Falcon Investment. The company's core business is developing "Mobility + Manipulation" physical AI models for heavy-duty scenarios, and it has already put more than 100 heavy trucks on 60 routes, mainly short-distance bulk material transfers of 0 to 300 kilometers. It has also run real-road zero-takeover tests in regions such as Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia.

The company's model architecture follows what it calls an AI-native paradigm, with a general multimodal pre-training base and a world model that generates training data and handles complex edge cases, followed by post-training and reinforcement learning aimed at rule compliance and safety. Its vehicle-side system, named TwinFast, pairs a JEV decision system for fast scenario judgment with an E2E end-to-end planning system that turns decisions into control actions, and the company says this addresses the slow reasoning speed of traditional high-level decision models. On data, EABOT reportedly adds more than 2 million new clips a month and has an automatic labeling scale above 100 million frames, supported by an operations team managing more than 100 vehicles and more than 100 drivers. CTO Li Wei, formerly head of algorithms at Inceptio, told Hard Krypton that the company plans to first run its own fleet to verify technology and costs, then sell "AI Driver Services" comprising vehicles, software and operating standards, and later extend the approach to excavators, loaders and mining operations.

Li Wei attributed the company's speed to a shift in technical paradigm away from rule-based autonomous driving toward AI-driven methods, which he said gives new entrants a chance to avoid the legacy of traditional architectures. He also pointed to physical AI positioning from the outset, data infrastructure built as a core capability, and the density of talent on the model team. The team's members come from Huawei, Li Auto, Momenta and Apple. The article does not say when the model will be deployed in vehicles beyond the subtitle's statement that it will be deployed within half a year, and it gives no further details on future funding or the company's next milestones.

Articles.Title: 36Kr Exclusive: Heavy-Duty Physical AI Startup Secures Nearly 400 Million Yuan Financing Within 1 Year of Establishment – Core Team Ex-Huawei & Li Auto, 100+ Vehicles in Operation - 36Kr

stories.Headline: China's 'potato capital' cultivates new crop of data centres as AI boom takes root - CNA
stories.Summary:
Ulanqab, a city in China's Inner Mongolia region known as the country's "potato capital," is rapidly turning its farmland into sites for AI data centres. Reporting by CNA visited the city, where the boom is changing local livelihoods and raising questions about water use in a drought-prone area. Farmer Zhang Zhiyong, 64, said developers began approaching residents of his village, Shengjiaying, about two years ago to buy land for data centres. He received more than 200,000 yuan (US$30,000) for about 0.7 hectares of his roughly 1.3 hectares, and now grows potatoes on just one mu, about 670 square metres.

Ulanqab has long been a major agricultural producer, with annual potato output approaching 4 million tonnes, nearly 5 per cent of China's total, according to People's Daily in 2023. Now a different industry is taking hold, as Xinhua reported in October that the city has signed 109 computing-centre projects. As of August, AI-focused computing made up more than 90 per cent of the city's total computing capacity. The city is part of China's "East Data, West Computing" strategy, which moves computing work from the more developed east to western areas with more land and energy.

President Xi Jinping visited the Chahar High-Tech Development Zone on October 16, a data-centre hub housing facilities run by Huawei, Alibaba and Apple. According to state media, Xi was briefed on green computing infrastructure and called for closer coordination between computing, electricity and water resources. Local officials and developers are responsible for the expansion, and the articles say the central leadership is paying close attention to it. Water sustainability in the drought-prone region remains a concern raised by the reporting.

The construction boom has also changed local business, with food vendors serving workers at the sites. Food hawker Gao Lina, 46, said she sells about 100 portions of pork rib rice a day at the Bayin data-centre cluster, and about 30 roadside eateries were seen operating nearby. Her stall moved there about a year ago, and she hopes to stay for another two to three years as more facilities are planned. At Yiwutang, a vendor said his customers have shifted from construction workers to engineers as building gives way to equipment installation.

Articles.Title: China's 'potato capital' cultivates new crop of data centres as AI boom takes root - CNA

stories.Headline: China's AI race is heating up. Can Tencent hold its ground? - CNA
stories.Summary:
Tencent, the Chinese internet giant behind the WeChat app, is facing growing pressure as artificial intelligence reshapes China's technology industry. The company has lost ground in short-form video and its AI chatbot Yuanbao trails rivals, including ByteDance's Doubao. According to analytics firm QuestMobile, Doubao had 382 million monthly active users in June, compared with about 50 million for Yuanbao. Investor concern over Tencent's AI strategy has also weighed on its Hong Kong-listed shares.

The competitive landscape is becoming more crowded and fragmented. Rui Ma, founder of Tech Buzz China, said the large number of companies in China's AI market makes it far more competitive than the United States, where she described the field as close to a duopoly between OpenAI and Anthropic. Analyst Pei Pei said the contest is shifting from a rivalry among established internet firms, such as Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu, toward a split between traditional tech companies that struggle to adapt, those that embrace AI and a new wave of AI startups. He pointed to developer Zhipu, which briefly passed HK$1 trillion, or US$128 billion, in market value in June.

Tencent has been more measured than its rivals in its AI push, and analysts and former staff describe its approach as deliberate and cautious. Former Tencent project manager Iris Jiang said the company generally has a less cut-throat culture than some competitors, and recalled advice from WeChat's lead developer, Zhang Xiaolong, to question a path when everyone is following it. Pei contrasted the leadership styles, saying ByteDance's founders were willing to commit substantial resources early, while Tencent's leaders, including CEO Pony Ma and President Martin Lau, were more reserved. Analyst Chen Zemin linked this caution to Tencent's "Tech for Good" philosophy and its focus on user value.

The articles suggest the outcome is uncertain. WeChat, which had more than 1.4 billion monthly active users across its Chinese and international versions at the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Tencent's gaming business could still give the company an edge. Yet analysts warn that AI could eventually take over some of the roles that platforms such as WeChat and Douyin play. Whether Tencent can adapt quickly enough as AI changes how people use technology remains the central question.

Articles.Title: China's AI race is heating up. Can Tencent hold its ground? - CNA

stories.Headline: Nasdaq set to confirm correction as AI spending worries mount - CNA
stories.Summary:
The Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 4 per cent on Thursday, November 5, 2026, closing in on a confirmed correction as worries about huge AI spending and closer scrutiny of data-center expansion rattled technology stocks. The index dropped to 24,712.60, more than 10 per cent below its record closing high of 27,599.89, set on October 6. The slide wiped out the previous session's gains, which had come after Democrats won both houses of Congress. A fall of 10 per cent from the latest record close is widely treated as a correction, and this would be the Nasdaq's second of the year.

October was already painful for the index, which lost more than $2.5 trillion in market value that month. Several large tech companies are borrowing in debt markets to help pay for billions of dollars in planned spending on data centers, chips and other infrastructure for AI development. Investors have been asking how soon that spending will turn into profits, especially since tensions in the Middle East and fears of lasting inflation have kept borrowing costs high. Earnings last month from Alphabet and Meta did not calm those doubts about returns, and they added to a wider selloff in AI-linked shares.

Sameer Samana, senior global market strategist at Wells Fargo Investment Institute, linked part of the move to the election result. He said a switch from one party holding unified control to the other can bring uncertainty, discontinuity and abrupt policy change. He added that when Democrats looked set to win big majorities in both the House and the Senate, his firm thought markets would at least take a short pause. Investors, the report said, were weighing the chance of tougher scrutiny of further AI infrastructure buildout.

The selloff has pushed money toward other parts of the market. According to Investing.com, investors have moved toward Chinese and Indian equities and Asian sectors less reliant on technology, after semiconductor-heavy markets fell sharply following the U.S. midterms. A Hong Kong index of mainland Chinese companies rose 5.2% last week, its best showing since March 2025, while India's Nifty 50 jumped 8.6%, its largest weekly gain since 2021. Overseas investors bought a net $1.9 billion of Indian shares through Wednesday, and in South Korea attention has turned to cosmetics, entertainment, retail and food firms. Some investors still see the AI downturn as a chance to buy, but the immediate trend favors diversifying into businesses with different earnings drivers.

Articles.Title: Nasdaq set to confirm correction as AI spending worries mount - CNA

stories.Headline: Big ticket tech deals needed to keep pace with AI growth boom, financial leaders say
stories.Summary:
Tech companies will need to complete more large fundraising deals to meet the huge demand for capital that the AI industry's growth boom is creating, global financial leaders said on Tuesday, Nov 3, at an investment gathering in Hong Kong. Jon Gray, president of Blackstone, said most major tech companies are expected to raise more capital because demand for computing power is running well ahead of supply. Combined AI-related spending is set to exceed US$730 billion this year, up from about US$700 billion, even as tech stocks have come under pressure in recent weeks over concerns about that spending. Gray cited equity raises by Meta, Google and Oracle, along with planned public listings by SpaceX and Anthropic.

Fundraising by Asia-Pacific tech companies more than tripled to US$125.8 billion in the first three quarters of 2026, up from US$36 billion a year earlier, according to LSEG data cited in the report. The growth was driven by semiconductor and AI-related deals, including the US$9.8 billion IPO of Chinese chipmaker CXMT and the US$910.6 million listing of Enflame Technology. Blackstone also agreed last week to provide US$63 billion of financing, arranged with Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, to help Anthropic buy Broadcom's AI chips and networking gear. Alphabet, the parent of Google, sold 6 billion euros (US$6.7 billion) of bonds on Monday, a test of investor appetite that the article describes as the latest.

Goldman Sachs chief executive David Solomon said strong companies with good stories would still be able to raise capital despite AI-related market turbulence, though the industry's growth could bring volatility for investors. Morgan Stanley chief executive Ted Pick warned of early signs that US markets were edging toward a correction, with most stocks in major indices down nearly 10 per cent. Gray said rising capital costs and current skepticism would slow the pace of deals, but he argued the overall trend points toward greater investment and a growing need for multiple forms of capital. PIMCO chief executive Emanuel Roman said AI financing deals are attractive and more are coming for his firm. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta have all signaled that their AI spending will not slow.

Articles.Title: Big ticket tech deals needed to keep pace with AI growth boom, financial leaders say - The Business Times

stories.Headline: China advances AI applications that add value to society: Argentine media expert - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
The Xinhua article reports that an Argentine media expert observed China putting artificial intelligence to work in ways that bring value to society. The piece, published on November 8, 2026, presents this view as the expert's assessment rather than as a news event with a specific trigger. It also notes his view that the growth of Chinese companies in the AI sector is helping to weaken the dominance of a small number of major players. According to the expert, this shift is fostering a more diverse ecosystem for the technology.

The article is short and does not list specific AI applications, products, companies, dates of policy changes, or figures. It does not describe any new rules, requirements, or changes that the expert attributes to the Chinese government or industry. The surrounding page links cover unrelated subjects such as autumn scenery, a trade fair pavilion, and the motorcycle market, which are not connected to the AI claims. Because the story rests on one commentator's observations, the article does not offer independent data to test those claims.

The only person quoted or identified is the Argentine media expert, whose remarks are summarized here without direct quotation. The article does not name him or describe his background beyond his nationality and field. Xinhua, China's state news agency, is the publisher, which is relevant context for readers weighing a commentary piece about China's domestic technology sector. The article offers no response from companies, regulators, or competitors, and it does not indicate whether further coverage or developments are expected.

Articles.Title: China advances AI applications that add value to society: Argentine media expert - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Investors see bright prospects for AI applications in China - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Investors at the 5th Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong said they see bright prospects for AI applications in China. The summit concluded on Wednesday, November 5, 2026. Zhang Lei, founder of Hillhouse Investment, spoke about the need for AI to deliver productivity. James Lydotes, chief investment officer of equities at a New York-based investment firm, told Xinhua that China is going to lead in physical AI.

Zhang said investors now expect AI to be applied in every industry, including manufacturing, health care, services and consumption. He said Asia will play a big role because it has more solid use cases than everywhere else. Lydotes said U.S. frontier labs and China are the biggest sources of AI innovation. He said he will be closely watching developments in factory automation in China to cash in on relevant investment.

China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said late last month that it is drafting policies for next-generation smart manufacturing. The measures aim to deepen the integration of artificial intelligence and manufacturing. They are meant to integrate AI across the entire manufacturing chain and develop new manufacturing models. The ministry said these models would help firms cut costs, raise efficiency and better meet diverse market demands.

The summit took place as the AI race enters what the article calls a "show me the money" phase, with calls for returns from mounting capital expenditure. Zhang tied this to productivity, saying AI has to have some productivity. Lydotes pointed to China's advanced manufacturing facility as the reason he expects it to lead in physical AI. The article does not say what happens next beyond the ministry's drafting of the policies.

Articles.Title: Investors see bright prospects for AI applications in China - Xinhua

stories.Headline: AI to drive next farming revolution
stories.Summary:
Chinese researchers are using artificial intelligence to speed up seed breeding, according to a China Daily report published on November 5, 2026. Sun Qixin, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and a professor at China Agricultural University, is using computer simulations to predict plant growth from genetic code. He said this could accelerate crop breeding by up to hundreds of times, compared with labor-intensive work once done in the field. Sun said the technology could mark the start of a fundamental revolution in agricultural breeding.

Sun said three foundations are needed for the change: more comprehensive agricultural data, lower-cost genetic sequencing and more sophisticated models linking a plant's genetic makeup to its observable traits. He said sequencing the genome of an individual wheat plant once cost around 1 million yuan, about $150,000, while comparable work now costs about 100 yuan. He expected that within three to five years, accumulated technical data on major grain crops and livestock could support specialized intelligent breeding models. He said AI could eventually take over as much as 80 percent of the workload in certain stages of conventional breeding, and that about five years may be needed before the practical impact becomes more widely visible.

Chen Wei, president of China Agricultural University, said the changing nature of agriculture is reshaping demand for talent and the priorities of agricultural universities. He said the university is adjusting its programs and research priorities under a medium- and long-term strategy for the next five to 10 years, and has introduced new programs including biological breeding and intelligent science and technology. He said agricultural technologies should be affordable and practical for farmers, and that their value depends not only on scientific breakthroughs but also on whether farmers can use them conveniently and effectively. Du Jinyi, from the national rural vitalization publicity and education center, said a workforce able to operate advanced equipment, interpret data and manage sophisticated production systems is in urgent need.

The 15th Five-Year Plan for accelerating agricultural and rural modernization, released in June, emphasizes emerging and future industries in agriculture, the first time such a focus has been explicitly included in a national planning document. It calls for scaling up technologies and industries including intelligent breeding, new-energy agricultural machinery, the low-altitude economy in agriculture, agricultural bio-manufacturing and novel foods. An official from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs said the initiatives are intended to foster new quality productive forces in agriculture, with measures including tax incentives for scientific and technological innovation. Qiu Tongwei, a professor at Nanjing Agricultural University, said emerging and future agricultural industries form the technological foundation of the country's strategy to become an agricultural powerhouse.

Articles.Title: AI to drive next farming revolution - China Daily

stories.Headline: What they passed on: AI reimagines 3 Long March stories from Chinese schoolbooks
stories.Summary:
The Global Times published a feature on November 8, 2026, in which an artificial intelligence project was used to reimagine three stories from the Long March, the 1934 to 1936 retreat of the Red Army. The articles say the stories have been kept alive through generations of Chinese school textbooks and remain widely remembered. The piece frames the work around the 90th anniversary of the march, marking nine decades since the Red Army completed what it describes as a remarkable feat. The stories were chosen because they are familiar to schoolchildren across the country.

The reimagined versions use AI to recreate scenes and characters from those textbook tales in new visual and narrative form. According to the article, the aim is to make the episodes accessible to younger readers who may not connect with the original printed accounts. The piece does not give exact figures for how many people took part or how many versions were produced. It describes the project as a way of carrying the spirit of the march forward to new generations.

The articles do not set out a formal rule or requirement attached to the work. The article attributes the project to the Global Times, which presents it as a cultural and educational initiative. It describes the work as a reflection on how the Long March is taught and remembered in China. The piece does not name individual creators or officials responsible for the AI reimagining.

Its tone is commemorative, presenting the anniversary as an occasion for renewed attention to the march. The Long March is a central episode in the history of the Chinese Communist Party and is regularly featured in national education. The articles do not describe any further publication plans, follow-up releases, or responses from outside groups. Beyond the anniversary framing, the articles say little about what comes next for the project.

Articles.Title: What they passed on: AI reimagines 3 Long March stories from Chinese schoolbooks - Global Times

stories.Headline: US political divisions cloud AI industry outlook, potentially affecting investment and global tech supply chains: analyst
stories.Summary:
The US artificial intelligence industry is facing growing political uncertainty after the Democrats won the midterm elections, with lawmakers preparing to scrutinize technology giants more closely and push for new rules. An analyst told the Global Times that deepening political divisions are spilling into the tech sector, as the two parties compete to shape how AI is developed and regulated. The analyst said that while the US remains a global leader in AI, these policy differences could create uncertainty over long-term investment and industry development. That uncertainty could also ripple across global supply chains and financial markets.
