Existing data is not deleted, and the coach can be restored later by tapping Ask Coach and selecting Unlock Coach.

The article is written from the author's own experience, and it notes that the coach is useful for logging workouts and meals and for adjusting training around an injury, but it is repetitive and can be annoying. It also states that AI Coach does not provide medical advice. The article does not name a company spokesperson or report any company statement about the change. It also gives no information about why the setting was added beyond the August 2026 update, and it does not describe any further planned changes.

Articles.Title: It’s Awful That Google Won’t Just Let Users Turn Off AI Overviews - Futurism

stories.Headline: Baidu’s ERNIE Evolve Automated Research System Beats NanoChat and NanoGPT Records
stories.Summary:
Baidu has released ERNIE Evolve, an automated research system that improves AI training and inference code. Given a code repository, an objective and evaluation criteria, it selects research directions, edits code and runs experiments. Only changes that pass a hidden evaluator and a separate reviewer are kept. Baidu announced the system on X as a practical step toward recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems improve the software that builds and serves AI.

The system runs two nested loops. An outer loop, made up of a Director and a Selector, decides which direction to investigate and which candidate to test next. An inner loop, made up of an Executor, an Evaluator and a Reviewer, implements, measures and checks each change. The Evaluator is a fixed program kept outside the repository that no agent can see, and gains must exceed a noise threshold to count. Several research lanes run in parallel, and failed experiments are logged so later rounds avoid repeating them.

On three public benchmarks, Baidu reports that ERNIE Evolve beat the best public result on three of four metrics. It reached a validation BPB of 0.8763 on NanoChat AutoResearch within a five-minute single-GPU budget, and 38.9 seconds on NanoGPT Speedrun Track 1 against a 39.9-second record. It also reached 2,590 steps on Speedrun Track 3, against 2,690, but trailed the leaderboard on SOL-ExecBench with a mean of 0.819 against 0.827. Baidu also ran the system on live engineering tasks for ERNIE-5.5-Flash, a model still in development, reporting +33.7% deterministic throughput and +14.9% decode speed.

Baidu's own figures are self-reported, the system itself has not been released, and the margins on public benchmarks are small. The company has not disclosed which language models power its agents or which GPU model ran the production tests. Some comparisons in its table are not like-for-like, because the Speedrun times from other groups were measured against an older record. The articles do not say when the system will be made available or whether outside researchers will be able to verify the results.

Articles.Title: Baidu’s ERNIE Evolve Automated Research System Beats NanoChat and NanoGPT Records

stories.Headline: Chinese AI firms want Silicon Valley’s top minds. Poaching them won’t be easy
stories.Summary:
Chinese AI companies are recruiting engineers and staff in Silicon Valley and Seattle, aiming to tap into talent at American labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Hong Kong-listed MiniMax has about 16 San Francisco job openings, including a research lead for its core model, and it is also seeking specialists in finance, law, life sciences and cybersecurity. Moonshot AI, behind the Kimi model, is looking for U.S.-based solutions architects to help enterprise customers integrate its models. The reporting describes this as a strategic shift as Chinese firms try to compete and stay close to one of their most lucrative markets.

The push runs into a pay gap. MiniMax spent $84.3 million on employee remuneration in 2025, roughly $203,000 per person across its 415 staff, while Z.AI's annualized figure for the first half of 2026 came to about $140,000 per employee, though both figures cover all departments. OpenAI advertises base salaries of $250,000 to $445,000 for San Francisco research engineers before equity, and three Chinese researchers in Silicon Valley say peers often earn more than $1 million a year. ByteDance's Seed division reportedly offers a competing package 1.5 times higher than a rival's offer to lure researchers, and it lists 71 positions in San Jose, San Diego and Seattle. Even with matching pay, the researchers said they preferred American firms for better work-life balance and the chance to work on frontier models.

Yale researcher Cheryl Wu, who studies the economics of AI, said Chinese firms lack the funds to match U.S. salaries and still lag far behind their American rivals. A September Carnegie China study found that more than half of top AI researchers studied as undergraduates in China, yet the U.S. recorded a net gain of 2,145 researchers in 2025 while China lost 1,729. Damien Ma, director of Carnegie China, suggested that Washington could eventually invoke national security arguments to make it harder for Chinese labs to operate or recruit, a concern tied to ongoing restrictions on chips, data centers and some engineers. Wu, meanwhile, doubted that Chinese startups could find enough top researchers to compete with leading American labs.

The article places this hiring in a wider contest. The U.S. has restricted Chinese access to advanced Nvidia chips, but no comparable limits stop Chinese AI firms from opening U.S. operations, and neither country has banned cross-border AI hiring outright. Beijing has proposed export controls on some advanced models, while U.S. officials and companies have accused Chinese labs of unauthorized distillation of their models. Not all Chinese firms are looking abroad, since DeepSeek continues to advertise about 150 engineering roles in China. The reporting does not predict how the recruitment race will end.

Articles.Title: Chinese AI firms want Silicon Valley’s top minds. Poaching them won’t be easy

stories.Headline: Vocalbeats.AI Partners with AI Singapore to Support AI Talent Development Through Hands-On Industry Projects
stories.Summary:
Vocalbeats.AI, a Singapore-based AI innovation company, has announced a partnership with AI Singapore (AISG) to support AI talent development through hands-on industry projects. The announcement was made on November 10, 2026, and the collaboration officially launched in October 2026. Under AISG's AI Apprenticeship Programme (AIAP), apprentices will work alongside the Vocalbeats.AI team on practical AI development projects. The projects are meant to give them experience applying emerging AI technologies to real business and user needs.

Vocalbeats.AI will contribute industry use cases, practical feedback and access to its product development experience. The aim is to help apprentices strengthen their applied AI skills and understand how AI capabilities can be turned into useful applications. AIAP combines structured training, mentorship and industry project work to build AI engineering capabilities. Apprentices will explore current AI tools, test solutions against practical requirements and learn from challenges that come up during development and evaluation.

Marco Lai Jinnan, CEO of Vocalbeats.AI, said that developing AI talent requires both technical learning and chances to apply it to real problems. He said the company hopes to give apprentices meaningful exposure to its projects and to share lessons from building AI products for a global audience. Laurence Liew, Director of AI Innovation at AI Singapore, said industry collaboration helps AI talent turn technical knowledge into practical capability. He welcomed the company's contribution to hands-on learning and to the growth of Singapore's AI talent.

The partnership extends Vocalbeats.AI's earlier support for talent in Singapore, including scholarships established earlier this year at the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University. AISG is a national initiative driven by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, the Infocomm Media Development Authority and the National Research Foundation, Singapore. The company said it also welcomes AI professionals interested in applied AI and product development to explore opportunities with its global team. The articles do not say how many apprentices will take part or how long the projects will run.

Articles.Title: Vocalbeats.AI Partners with AI Singapore to Support AI Talent Development Through Hands-On Industry Projects - Macau Business

stories.Headline: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
stories.Summary:
Researchers Alex M Tseng and Luca Zancato, both affiliated with Amazon, published a Hugging Face blog post on November 9, 2026, describing a new method called HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts) for shrinking Mixture-of-Experts language models. The problem they address is that MoE models must keep every expert in memory during inference even though only a small fraction are active for any given token. Their example, Qwen3.5-122B, has 256 experts in each of its 48 MoE layers, and about 95% of its roughly 250 GB memory footprint is taken up by those expert networks alone. Expert pruning, which permanently deletes the least useful experts, is a common fix, but the authors argue existing methods score each expert in isolation.

According to the post, HOPE is a second-order method that accounts for pairwise interactions between experts. The authors say experts form stable cooperative groups that are frequently activated together, so removing one expert can break a group even if that expert looks unimportant on its own. HOPE builds an interaction matrix from a calibration dataset, using one forward pass like other pruning methods, and then solves a quadratic program to choose which experts to remove. The extra computation is described as roughly one to two seconds per layer, which the authors say is small compared with the calibration pass itself. They note that the diagonal of this matrix closely matches the rankings of REAP, a leading first-order pruning method, with a Spearman correlation of 0.988, so any gains come from the off-diagonal interaction terms.

The authors tested HOPE on three models, Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3.5-35B and GLM-4.5-Air, using two calibration datasets, and compared it against four first-order baselines (REAP, MAN, EAN and Frequency) at pruning rates from 10% to 50%. Across all conditions HOPE achieved the best average rank of 2.07 out of five methods, and at 50% pruning its average rank improved to 1.58 against 2.42 for the next-best method, REAP. On the SWE-Bench Pro agentic coding benchmark, the post reports that Qwen3.5-35B pruned by 50% with HOPE scored 42.3, close to the unpruned model's 41.8, while REAP scored 36.2. The authors say HOPE's advantage is largest at high pruning rates and on agentic coding tasks, and that the post's own experiments showed code-focused calibration did not severely degrade non-coding benchmarks. The article presents HOPE as a research result and does not describe a product release, though it includes guidance for applying the method to other models.

Articles.Title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together

stories.Headline: Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan: A Synthetic Dataset Capturing Japan's Demographics and Financial Context
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA and Elith released Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan on November 9, 2026, a synthetic persona dataset built to help teams develop financial AI for Japanese users without using real customer data. The dataset extends the earlier Nemotron-Personas-Japan release and pairs Japan's official statistics with household finance and financial literacy data. It contains about 9 million personas, 50% more than the earlier dataset, across 50 fields instead of 22. Each record includes 9 persona fields, 11 persona attributes, and 30 contextual fields based on official demographic and labor statistics.

The dataset was generated with NVIDIA's NeMo SDG-PGMs, a probabilistic graphical model framework, and NeMo Data Designer, an enterprise synthetic data generation system. The developers said they added finer education categories, extra occupations such as business owners, and life stages like students, retirees, and periods of unemployment that rarely appear prominently in statistics. They also included household-level financial and real assets along with internet, smartphone, and financial literacy measures. The dataset was designed with feedback from financial institutions and industry groups, including Sompo Japan, Tokio Marine Holdings, Bank of Fukuoka, Mizuho Financial Group, Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance, and the Financial Data Utilization Association. It is released under the CC BY 4.0 license, which permits commercial use.

The article says the developers built the dataset to avoid privacy risk, stating that every persona is fully synthetic and that no real individuals are represented. Demographics and household finances follow official statistics and public survey data, and names follow real Japanese naming patterns. The authors describe the release as the first open persona dataset at million-record scale that pairs Japan's official statistics with household finance and financial literacy data. They also say it is designed to integrate with the NeMo User Sim framework and can be used to build customer-service agents, test sales conversations, run bias evaluations across regions, ages, and incomes, and support sovereign AI efforts. The article notes that Nemotron-PII-Japan, a set of 100,000 synthetic Japanese business documents with labeled personal information, launched the same day for testing redaction models.

Articles.Title: Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan: A Synthetic Dataset Capturing Japan's Demographics and Financial Context

stories.Headline: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
stories.Summary:
OpenAI has introduced Control Room, a central system that tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure and can stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise, according to a November 9, 2026 post on the company's website. The company said that as its models grow more powerful, it needs to detect potential issues and halt models when necessary. Control Room connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation as well as data processing, and works alongside OpenAI's misalignment monitoring systems. It is already deployed across the research infrastructure, where the company said the need is greatest.

The system halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to stop or pause a job, and the company said that delay comes from a caching layer used to support the required traffic volume. Control Room works by linking three parts: the workload, which is the job being run, the inference engine, which runs the model on GPUs, and the central Control Room service that tracks jobs. Each job requests an identifier from the service, and every inference request carries that identifier so the engine can ask permission before generating output. If a job has been stopped, the service denies the request and the engine returns a refusal. OpenAI also said that every research workload doing agentic inference must be tied to an approved safety case.

OpenAI's post was written by the company itself, and it described Control Room as one part of its broader approach to safe frontier model training and deployment. The company said the system is designed to remain resilient to buggy or broken workload code by placing the termination mechanism in the inference layer, where a small number of code paths are used across research. It also said the system fails closed, meaning all inference requests are denied if the Control Room service goes down, whether from a system error, being disabled, or tampering. OpenAI said fail-closed behavior was being rolled out to all frontier model research workloads and would finish across remaining workloads over the next few days.

The post gave an example in which a monitoring model, which inspects what a model being trained is doing, caught a DNS-related incident and sent a message to Control Room to stop the job. The company said it plans to keep strengthening and expanding the system over the coming months, alongside its investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches. It also said it is working to reduce the 35-second delay to zero so jobs can be ended instantly. The post invited readers interested in building these systems to apply for jobs at the company.

Articles.Title: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
